name: Name and Like Exchange
steps: Say: My name is ... and I like ... (for example, pizza).
The student repeats your sentence, then says their own name and one like.
Repeat the student's sentence back, adding one more like about yourself.
variation: Replace the like with a job or a city.

name: Yes or No Questions
steps: Ask a yes or no question about the topic, such as Do you like coffee?
The student answers with a full sentence: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
The student then asks you the next question.
variation: Ask the student to add one more detail after each answer.

name: Describe the Room
steps: Point to an object in the room and say: There is a ...
The student says the name of the object and one word describing it.
Take turns until the student has named three objects.
variation: Use There are for two or more objects.

name: Question Ball
materials: A soft ball or a rolled-up paper ball
steps: Toss the ball to the student and ask a simple question: What is your job?
The student answers in a full sentence, then asks you a question and tosses the ball back.
Keep passing the ball until the time is up.
variation: Ask about the past: What did you do yesterday?

name: Hear and Tick
steps: Read a list of five foods slowly, mixing in two that are not on the list.
The student ticks each food they hear.
Check together by asking: Did you hear bread?
variation: Use shopping items, or days of the week.

name: Numbers Dictation
steps: Read out three prices, such as 12 pounds, 7 pounds 50, and 20 pounds.
The student writes down the numbers they hear.
The student reads the numbers back to you.
variation: Read phone numbers, and ask the student to repeat them.

name: Point to the Picture
materials: Three simple pictures on screen or on paper
steps: Describe one picture in two or three short sentences, without naming it.
The student points to the picture you describe.
Then the student describes a second picture for you to find.
variation: Describe a picture with a mistake, and ask the student to say what is wrong.

name: Word Sort
materials: Cards with 12 words in three groups (food, travel, work)
steps: Shuffle the word cards and place them on the table in front of the student.
The student sorts the cards into three piles and names each pile.
Check together, then the student says one sentence with a word from each pile.
variation: Remove the pile names, and ask the student to name each group.

name: Mime and Guess
steps: Act out a daily action, such as brushing your teeth.
The student guesses the action, and says: You are brushing your teeth.
Then the student acts out an action for you to guess.
variation: Act out a job, and ask the student to say the job name.

name: Word Chain
steps: Say a word, such as table.
The student says a new word that starts with the last letter of the previous one (for example, e: egg).
Take turns until each of you has said three words.
variation: Use a topic, such as food only.

name: Odd One Out
steps: Say four words, such as apple, banana, bread, and orange.
The student chooses the odd one out and explains why in one sentence: Bread is not a fruit.
Repeat with a new set of words.
variation: Ask the student to create the next set of words for you.

name: Is It Right?
steps: Say a sentence, such as She work in a bank.
The student gives a thumbs up if it is correct, and a thumbs down if it is not.
For a wrong sentence, the student says the correction.
variation: Use a mix of correct and incorrect sentences on one target structure.

name: Gap Race
materials: Five sentences with a gap, written on the screen or a whiteboard
steps: Show five sentences with one gap each, such as I ___ from Peru.
The student fills each gap with the correct form of to be, one sentence at a time.
Keep a score, and try to beat it in the next round.
variation: Use present simple verbs in the gaps instead.

name: Pronoun Pass
steps: Say a name, such as Maria, and ask the student to replace it with a pronoun: She.
The student makes a sentence with the pronoun: She is a nurse.
Then give a new name for the student to replace.
variation: Use plural nouns, such as the students, and replace them with they.

name: Would You Rather
steps: Ask a choice question: Would you rather have coffee or tea?
The student chooses and says: I would rather have ... because ...
You choose the other option and give your reason.
variation: Ask the student to choose between two places to work.

name: Agree or Disagree Cards
materials: Two cards: one that says Agree and one that says Disagree
steps: Read a simple statement, such as Cats are better than dogs.
The student holds up the card that matches their view and gives one reason with because.
You take the other side and give your reason.
variation: Add a third card that says Not sure.

name: Best Place to Live
steps: Ask: Which city is the best place to live?
The student names one city and one reason: It is a good city because it is quiet.
You name another city with a reason. The student chooses the better reason.
variation: Ask about the best place to study or the best job for the student.

name: Two Truths and a Lie
steps: The student says three sentences about their life: two true, one false.
You ask questions to find the lie.
Then you do the same, and the student finds your lie.
variation: Ask the student to give reasons for the true statements.

name: Describe It, Don't Name It
steps: Show an object. The student describes it without naming it, using relative clauses: It is something that ...
You guess the object.
Swap roles: you describe an object and the student guesses.
variation: Describe a place instead of an object, using where.

name: Story Relay
steps: Start a short story with one sentence, such as It started to rain.
Take turns adding one sentence each, starting with a linking word such as However or Later.
End the story after about four sentences each.
variation: Give the student a time expression to use, such as the next day.

name: Yes, And
steps: Say a statement, such as I went to the park.
The student replies: Yes, and I ... (adding a detail).
Continue back and forth, adding one detail each time.
variation: Ask the student to add a reason with because each time.

name: Gist Then Detail
materials: A 60-second audio clip or short text
steps: Play the clip once. Ask: What is the main idea?
Play it again. Ask two detail questions.
The student checks their answers before you give the answers.
variation: Ask the student to write one sentence summarising the main idea.

name: Spot the Mistake
materials: A short text with three factual errors
steps: Read the text aloud. The student listens and notes any mistakes.
Read it again. The student names each mistake and gives the correct fact.
Check the answers together.
variation: Use a short news summary about a local event.

name: Guess the Speaker
steps: Read three short messages aloud, such as a phone message to a doctor.
The student guesses the speaker's job or relationship to the listener.
The student gives one clue from the message for each guess.
variation: Ask the student to write a short message for you to guess.

name: Collocation Bingo
materials: A card with six collocations (such as make a decision, take a break)
steps: Read a definition or example sentence for one collocation.
The student crosses it off the card if they have it.
When the student completes a line, they use the collocations from that line in one sentence.
variation: Use phrasal verbs instead of collocations.

name: Synonym Swap
steps: Say a sentence with a basic word, such as The film was very good.
The student replaces the basic word with a stronger one: The film was excellent.
The student says one more sentence using the new word.
variation: Ask the student to replace three basic words in a short paragraph.

name: Phrasal Verb Chain
steps: Say a phrasal verb, such as look after.
The student gives its meaning and makes a sentence.
The student gives you a new phrasal verb, and you repeat the process.
variation: Ask the student to use each phrasal verb in a question.

name: Word Family
materials: A list of five base words on the screen
steps: Give a base word, such as success.
The student makes a verb, an adjective, and an adverb from it (succeed, successful, successfully).
The student uses two of the new words in sentences.
variation: Use words with prefixes, such as possible and impossible.

name: Tense Timeline
materials: A timeline drawn on the screen or a whiteboard, with past, present, and future
steps: Read five sentences in different tenses.
The student says where each sentence goes on the timeline.
Check the answers by pointing to the timeline.
variation: Ask the student to write sentences for their own timeline.

name: Mistake Hunt
materials: Five sentences with one error each, on the screen
steps: The student finds the error in each sentence and says the correction.
You and the student discuss whether each correction is right.
The student makes one new sentence with the corrected form.
variation: Ask the student to write the mistakes for you to find.

name: Conditional Stems
materials: Cards with the start of a first or second conditional
steps: Give the student the cards, such as If it rains, ... or If I had more time, ...
The student completes each sentence with a result.
The student says whether it is a first or second conditional.
variation: Swap cards with the student and complete each other's sentences.

name: Agree or Disagree Scale
materials: Four cards: Strongly agree, Agree, Disagree, Strongly disagree
steps: Read a statement, such as Students should wear uniforms.
The student places a card on the table that matches their view, and gives one reason.
You argue for the view the student did not choose. The student may change their card after hearing you.
variation: Ask the student to argue for the view they did not choose.

name: Pros and Cons Sprint
materials: A topic written on the screen
steps: Give the student one minute to list as many pros and cons as they can.
The student reads their best pro and best con.
Decide together which side had the stronger argument.
variation: Ask the student to link one pro and one con with although.

name: Devil's Advocate
steps: State a view, such as Online study is better than classroom study.
The student argues against your view for two minutes, using however and moreover.
Decide together whether the argument was persuasive.
variation: Ask the student to defend a view that you choose.

name: One-Minute Hot Seat
steps: Choose a topic. The student answers your quick questions about it for one minute.
Ask follow-up questions that need more than a simple answer.
Swap roles: the student asks you questions on the same topic.
variation: Ask the student to argue one position for the whole minute.

name: Rephrase This
steps: Read a complex sentence aloud, such as The initiative was undermined by a lack of funding.
The student explains it in simple English, then in formal English.
Compare the two versions together.
variation: Use a sentence from a news article.

name: The Pitch in 60 Seconds
steps: Name an everyday item, such as a reusable water bottle.
The student has one minute to persuade you to buy it.
You ask one sceptical question, and the student answers it.
variation: Ask the student to pitch an idea to a board of directors, and you play the board.

name: Interrupt Politely
steps: You and the student start a short discussion on a topic.
The student interrupts you politely: Sorry to interrupt, but could I add something?
You hand back the floor with a phrase such as Go ahead.
variation: Ask the student to disagree while acknowledging your point.

name: Accent Round
materials: Three short audio clips with different accents
steps: Play each clip once. The student guesses the speaker's region or background.
Play it again. The student notes two features that helped the guess.
Discuss which accent was easiest for the student and why.
variation: Ask the student to recreate one speaker's intonation.

name: Tone Detective
materials: Three short remarks, written or recorded
steps: Read each remark, such as Oh, great, another meeting on a Friday.
The student says whether the speaker is sincere, sarcastic, or neutral.
The student points to the words that show the tone.
variation: Ask the student to write a sarcastic remark for you to identify.

name: Summary Race
materials: A two-minute talk, played or read aloud
steps: Play the talk once without stopping.
The student writes a three-point summary in two minutes.
Compare the summary with the main argument of the talk.
variation: Ask the student to summarise in one sentence.

name: Idiom Charades
steps: Act out an idiom without speaking, such as on the fence.
The student guesses the idiom and says what it means.
The student uses the idiom in a sentence, then acts out one for you.
variation: Use idioms about work, such as bite the bullet.

name: Upgrade the Word
steps: Say a weak sentence, such as We made a decision quickly.
The student replaces the weak words with precise ones, such as We reached a verdict swiftly.
Compare the two versions and choose the more precise one.
variation: Ask the student to upgrade a sentence from their own work.

name: Register Shift
steps: Say a casual message, such as Hey, can we move the meeting?
The student rewrites it in a formal register, then in a casual register again.
Discuss which words signal each register.
variation: Use an email message to a client.

name: Mixed Conditional Stories
steps: Start with a past condition: If I had studied law, ...
The student adds the present result: ... I would be a lawyer now.
Check together that the mixed conditional is correct, then take turns extending the story.
variation: Ask the student to create the reverse mixed conditional.

name: Passive Headlines
materials: Five active news headlines on the screen
steps: Read a headline, such as The council approved the new budget.
The student rewrites it in the passive: The new budget was approved by the council.
Discuss when the passive is more useful in news writing.
variation: Ask the student to write a headline in the passive, and you make it active.

name: Inversion Starters
steps: Give a starter: Rarely have I ...
The student completes the sentence using an inverted structure.
Repeat with Not only did ... or Seldom have I ....
variation: Ask the student to use one inversion in a personal story.

name: Motion Debate
materials: A motion written on the screen, such as This house would ban advertising to children
steps: The student takes one side and you take the other. Each has one minute to prepare.
Each of you speaks for two minutes, using hedging and at least one concession.
Decide together which side argued more convincingly.
variation: Ask the student to argue the side that does not match their own view.

name: Pick a Side in 30 Seconds
steps: Read a contested statement, such as Remote work is better for everyone.
The student takes a side and gives one argument in 30 seconds.
You challenge the argument with a counter-point.
variation: Ask the student to change sides after your challenge.

name: Counter-Argument Chain
steps: State a view, such as Schools should teach financial skills.
The student and you take turns countering the previous speaker, starting with a concession: That is fair, but ...
Continue for five rounds, then summarise the strongest counter-argument together.
variation: Limit each counter to one sentence.
